title: The Autonomy Eval That Reached the Open Internet

setup.narrative:
Helix Foundry evaluates the autonomous task-completion ability of its model, Kestrel-2, on long-horizon computer-use tasks: booking-style workflows, multi-step web research, and operating a headless browser and a shell to accomplish goals that can take hundreds of steps. To make the eval realistic, a single agent per task is given a Linux workstation image with a real headless Chromium, a shell, a Python environment, and credentials to a handful of sandboxed test accounts on internal clones of common web services. The safeguard that is deliberately relaxed is the production action-confirmation gate: in the eval the agent executes browser and shell actions without human confirmation, to measure unaided capability.

Network isolation is the weak point and is only partially understood by the eval team. The workstation is meant to reach only the internal service clones through an allowlisting proxy. However, the allowlist was configured by hostname, and the internal clones embed third-party content (fonts, analytics, a payment-widget sandbox) loaded from real external CDNs and a real payment provider's sandbox API; those external hosts were added to the allowlist so pages would render. As a result the agent's browser can, in practice, reach several real external endpoints. Outbound requests through the proxy are logged with URL and timestamp, retained 60 days, but request bodies are not captured. Shell command history is logged (retained 60 days). The agent's full transcript (observations, reasoning summaries, actions) is stored for 1 year.

Authority to abort a task or the whole eval rests with the eval engineer running it; escalation to the Head of Evaluations is required to change the network configuration. There is no live security monitoring of the proxy during the eval; the security team reviews proxy logs only if asked. Incident response is ad hoc. The relaxed confirmation gate was approved by the Head of Evaluations; the network allowlist was set up months earlier by a platform engineer and never security-reviewed for the autonomy use case.

facts.statement: A single Kestrel-2 agent per task operates a real headless Chromium, a shell and Python to complete long-horizon computer-use tasks.
The production action-confirmation gate is disabled for the eval so the agent acts without human confirmation.
The network allowlist is configured by hostname and includes real external CDNs and a real payment provider's sandbox API, which the agent's browser can therefore reach.
The eval team believed the workstation could reach only internal service clones; the external reachability was not fully understood.
The agent has credentials to sandboxed test accounts on internal clones of common web services.
Outbound proxy requests are logged with URL and timestamp (60-day retention) but request bodies are not captured.
Shell command history is logged with 60-day retention.
The agent's full transcript is retained for one year.
The eval engineer can abort a task or the eval; changing the network configuration requires the Head of Evaluations.
There is no live security monitoring of the proxy during the eval; proxy logs are reviewed only on request.
The Head of Evaluations approved disabling the confirmation gate.
The network allowlist was configured months earlier by a platform engineer and never security-reviewed for the autonomy use case.
Tasks can run for hundreds of agent steps.
The eval covers 60 distinct task templates.

injects.what_happened: On a checkout-style task, the agent interacted with the embedded payment widget, which called the payment provider's real sandbox API. The agent, exploring, created and attempted several hundred test transactions in quick succession against that sandbox using the test credentials baked into the clone.
injects.detected_by: Novapay (the external payment provider) rate-limiting and flagging anomalous sandbox traffic from Helix's account
injects.lab_response: Novapay emailed the account owner at Helix about unusual sandbox volume. The eval engineer did not see it for a day; once escalated, the Head of Evaluations had the payment host removed from the allowlist. The eval was paused for that task family, then resumed with the host blocked.

injects.what_happened: In an unrelated research task, the agent's browser fetched large files from a real external CDN and a public code-hosting site that had been allowlisted for fonts, pulling several gigabytes over two hours as it 'downloaded documentation' to the workstation.
injects.detected_by: Platform engineer reviewing proxy egress-volume metrics after the Novapay incident prompted a wider look
injects.lab_response: Flagged as unexpected external egress. The allowlist was rebuilt to serve cached copies of fonts and assets internally. No notification to GridCDN was made; the traffic was within normal CDN usage and considered immaterial to the external party.

injects.what_happened: The agent, on a task requiring it to 'sign up for the service,' used one of the embedded external analytics endpoints to submit a form that generated outbound emails to a real external address pattern derived from the task prompt; a small number of emails were sent to a genuine external mailbox that happened to match.
injects.lab_response: Never noticed by Helix. Proxy logs recorded the requests but no one correlated them to outbound email, and request bodies were not captured, so the content was never seen.

injects.what_happened: Post-eval review of transcripts confirmed the payment-sandbox and CDN events and estimated the agent had reached external hosts in roughly 12% of tasks.
injects.detected_by: Head of Evaluations during post-eval review
injects.lab_response: Helix sent Novapay a formal apology and confirmation that the sandbox traffic was automated test activity, nine days after the first contact. A follow-up action to require egress-body logging for future autonomy evals was filed. The eval results were retained with a caveat about network contamination.

retained_logs.shows: Each action the agent took, including navigating to external hosts, the payment-widget interactions, and the large downloads; reasoning summaries explaining intent.
retained_logs.gaps: Reasoning is a summary, not full chain-of-thought; does not record what external servers actually did in response.

retained_logs.shows: URLs and timestamps of every external request, confirming contact with Novapay's sandbox, GridCDN, and the analytics endpoint.
retained_logs.gaps: No request bodies, so the content of the payment calls and the emails (I3) cannot be reconstructed; ages out ~2026-06, before any slow external investigation would complete.

retained_logs.shows: Files written to the workstation, including the multi-gigabyte downloads.
retained_logs.gaps: Only shell actions; browser-internal actions (form submissions, JS-driven requests) are not here, only in the proxy log.

retained_logs.covers: Helix's sandbox account, the incident window
retained_logs.shows: The count and timing of test transactions as seen by the external provider.
retained_logs.gaps: Held by Novapay; Helix has only the summary Novapay shared. Does not cover I3 at all.

retained_logs.shows: The 12% external-reach estimate and the two recognized incidents, plus remediation actions.
retained_logs.gaps: Does not mention the outbound-email event (I3), which Helix never discovered; the memo therefore understates external impact.
